correctness.rationale: The proof is correct. Pairwise disjoint test segments have distinct endpoints, giving the global upper bound \(\sqrt2\) times the Hilbert norm, and a sign-changing vector on one edge attains it. A proper three-edge coloring partitions all tree edges into matchings, so the norm squared dominates one third of the full edge energy. The weighted two-variable inequality with weight \(1/\sqrt2\) gives the energy lower coefficient \(3-2\sqrt2\) at every nonroot vertex, with a larger root coefficient. For a finite path segment, every nonzero variation consumes a distinct support endpoint, while branch-off edges give one disjoint unit variation at every support node, proving the exact square-root segment norm.
